items.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022
items.q: Now we’re talking from October to December. So I did that album and then started the “Leprechaun” in December of that year, ’75. ... going into that and working with Chick. ... we did this project together

ctx.x: Yeah, I must insert that I was living in Buffalo at the time and someone gave me tickets to see The Mahavishnu Orchestra, and I didn’t know what or who they were, and wow. I was totally blown away by that.

Yeah it wasn’t just precision and it wasn’t just technical expertise it was using that to create beautiful communication and interplay between the guys and it was at a high level. So anyway so I enjoyed that, and so I was in that mindset and was still doing you know rock dates and then the next thing that happens is in ’74 Stanley Clarke comes in to do his recording, do an album. I think it was his second album. And so I did some assisting on that and the engineer, Ken Scott, a great engineer, said, “Listen I…

doing. And she was expressing her music via her sense of poetry and so forth, and she was working with some other musicians. But it was basically rock. It was the beginnings of punk rock. So it wasn’t something that I had been digesting at all. It was something new for me. But I got into the game of it and I was just having fun. It was just fun.
